We argue that leveraging the information of attention maps across different layers is helpful for a comprehensive measurement of token similarity. Based on this idea, we first present PFA, which links the attention maps between adjacent layers using the Hadamard product, allowing the network to utilize the information of all previous attention layers. PFA can highlight the attention of relevant tokens while avoiding unnecessary computation on irrelevant ones. Second, we design a Window-based Progressive Focused Attention (WPFA) and a Group-based Progressive Focused Attention (GPFA) to implement PFA based on local spatial adjacency and global feature similarity. This architecture allows PFTv2 to focus on the most relevant tokens in both local and global contexts. Third, we propose the PFT-SGN framework, which applies PFA to multi-resolution branches for hierarchical attention focusing and cross-scale feature interaction in image restoration. Extensive experiments on single image super-resolution, Gaussian image denoising, real image denoising, JPEG compression artifact reduction, and all-in-one image restoration demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method across a broad range of image restoration tasks.

title: DOME: A Decoupled Offline-Online Memory Externalization Framework for Interpretable Domain-Generalized Face Anti-spoofing
abstract: Interpretable Face Anti-Spoofing (FAS) for Domain Generalization (DG) is becoming increasingly popular. However, despite the promise of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) in providing interpretability, current approaches suffer from a fundamental limitation: interpretable knowledge is implicitly coupled within model parameters. Consequently, the explanation process often degenerates into a post-hoc rationalization of prediction results rather than serving as the reasoning basis for decision-making. This “black-box” coupling not only severs the pathway for correcting visual biases via explicit logic but also necessitates extensive supervision to align interpretation with classification. To address these challenges, we propose the Decoupled Offline-online Memory Externalization (DOME) framework, which employs a vision-language bank to explicitly represent this implicit knowledge, ensuring predictions are derived from pre-retrieved evidence. Specifically, DOME is designed as a structured repository containing textual rules and visual prototypes. Our method operates in two stages: (1) Offline Memory Bank Construction, where we populate the memory by extracting rules and aggregating prototypes via a decision tree on a few training samples; and (2) Online Memory Interaction, where a trainable fusion module retrieves the stored rules from the memory as prior evidence for the MLLM, while enhancing features via the memory’s visual prototypes. By externalizing knowledge into the memory, our approach not only transforms explanations from passive outputs into active predictive priors but also liberates knowledge acquisition from massive supervision. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves competitive performance on multiple DG protocols while providing structured explanations.

title: SEE: See Everything Every Time - Adaptive Brightness Adjustment for Broad Light Range Images via Events
abstract: Abstract Event cameras, with a high dynamic range exceeding 120 dB , significantly outperform traditional embedded cameras, robustly recording detailed changing information under various lighting conditions, including both low- and high-light situations. However, recent research on utilizing event data has primarily focused on low-light image enhancement, neglecting image enhancement and brightness adjustment across a broader range of lighting conditions, such as normal or high illumination. Based on this, we propose a novel research question: how to employ events to enhance and adaptively adjust the brightness of images captured under broad lighting conditions? To investigate this question, we first collected a new dataset, SEE-600K, consisting of 610,126 images and corresponding events across 202 scenarios, each featuring an average of four lighting conditions with over a 1000-fold variation in illumination. Subsequently, we propose a framework that effectively utilizes events to smoothly adjust image brightness through the indication of custom brightness via user-introduced prompts. Our framework captures color through sensor patterns, uses cross-attention to model events as a brightness dictionary, and adjusts the image’s dynamic range to form a broad light-range representation (BLR), which is then decoded at the pixel level based on the user-introduced brightness prompt. Experimental results demonstrate that our method not only performs well on the low-light enhancement dataset but also shows robust performance on broader light-range image enhancement using the SEE-600K dataset. Additionally, our approach enables pixel-level brightness adjustment, providing flexibility for post-processing and inspiring more imaging applications. The dataset and source code are publicly available at: https://github.com/yunfanLu/SEE.

title: Fix Your Downsampling ASAP! Aliasing and Sinc Artifact Free Pooling in the Fourier Domain
abstract: Abstract Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are successful in various computer vision tasks. From an image and signal processing point of view, this success is counter-intuitive, as the inherent spatial pyramid design of most CNNs is apparently violating basic signal processing laws, i.e. the Sampling Theorem in their downsampling operations. This issue has been broadly neglected until recent work in the context of adversarial attacks and distribution shifts showed that there is a strong correlation between the vulnerability of CNNs and aliasing artifacts induced by bandlimit-violating downsampling. As a remedy, we propose an alias-free downsampling operation in the frequency domain, denoted Frequency Low Cut Pooling (FLC Pooling) which we further extend to Aliasing and Sinc Artifact-free Pooling (ASAP) . ASAP is alias-free and removes further artifacts from sinc-interpolation. Our experimental evaluation on ImageNet-1k, ImageNet-C and CIFAR datasets on various CNN architectures demonstrates that networks using FLC Pooling and ASAP as downsampling methods learn more stable features as measured by their robustness against common corruptions and adversarial attacks, while maintaining a clean accuracy similar to the respective baseline models.

title: Controllable Human-Object Interaction Synthesis via Progressive and Invertible Condition Injection
abstract: Controllable Human-Object Interaction synthesis aims to generate realistic HOI motions while ensuring all the given control constraints are exactly satisfied. Existing methods primarily generate the entire sequence with all control signals aggressively fused as input conditions in a single stage. However, these methods have significant limitations in satisfying multiple heterogeneous constraints while synthesizing realistic, detailed interactions all at once, which typically results in suboptimal generation performance. In this work, we propose PICI, a novel progressive HOI synthesis framework that generates realistic HOI sequences with different control constraints stage by stage, while keeping the cross-stage invertibility to enhance the generation consistency. Specifically, our PICI includes a sparse HOI generator that produces motion satisfying trajectory constraints and roughly aligning with text semantics, followed by a series of invertible infilling blocks that progressively refine the motion with additional interaction details, conditioned on the knowledge acquired in earlier stages. To better exploit the learned knowledge and facilitate progressive infilling, a Cross-density Knowledge Augmented Memory (CKAMem) is formulated to incrementally aggregate motion features throughout the generation process to facilitate coherent and realistic interactions. Combining these designs, our framework effectively enables the progressive generation of realistic and coherent interactions under multiple control constraints. We conduct extensive experiments on the FullBodyManipulation, 3D-FUTURE and InterAct Datasets, and the results demonstrate that our PICI framework outperforms the current state-of-the-art approaches.

title: AdaEA++: Enhanced Adaptive Model Ensemble Adversarial Attack for Boosting Adversarial Transferability
abstract: Transferability of adversarial examples enables black-box attacks without knowledge of victim model parameters and has drawn significant attention. Previous works mostly study gradient variation or image transformations to amplify the distortion on critical parts of inputs. These approaches transfer effectively across similar convolutional neural networks but struggle with heterogeneous architectures, such as vision transformers. Alternatively, model ensemble adversarial attacks have been proposed to fuse outputs from several surrogate models, which can make the generated adversarial example more likely to transfer to other models as it can fool multiple models concurrently. However, existing ensemble attacks generally fuse the outputs of the surrogate models evenly and thus do not explicitly exploit and amplify the intrinsic transfer information of adversarial examples. In this paper, we extend the conference-version AdaEA into AdaEA++. The central methodological advance of AdaEA++ is AGM++, a trajectory-decoupled weighting strategy that estimates input-conditioned surrogate contributions at the initial attack state and reuses them during subsequent optimization, thereby separating model-contribution estimation from the attack trajectory that it induces. Two complementary methodological refinements improve the reliability of this adaptive ensemble: RIE conditions all surrogate models on a shared masked view, while DRF++ replaces pixel-wise disparity estimation with neighborhood-aware gradient consensus. Together, these designs address temporal feedback, spatially unstable evidence, and local gradient misalignment in heterogeneous surrogate ensembles. As a result, AdaEA++ improves the average ASR from 46.90 to \(68.16\%\) on NIPS2017 and from 58.68 to \(68.80\%\) on the full ImageNet-1K validation set, while maintaining strong transferability on ImageNet-C and ImageNet-A. The proposed AdaEA++ can also boost existing transfer-based attacks, which further demonstrates its efficacy and versatility. The code and data related to our study will be available after publication.

title: DreamMix: Decoupling Object Attributes for Enhanced Editability in Customized Image Inpainting
abstract: Subject-driven image inpainting has recently gained prominence in image editing with the rapid advancement of diffusion models. Beyond image guidance, recent studies have explored incorporating text guidance to achieve identity-preserved yet locally editable object inpainting. However, these methods still suffer from identity overfitting, where original attributes remain entangled with target textual instructions. To overcome this limitation, we propose DreamMix, a diffusion-based framework adept at inserting target objects into user-specified regions while concurrently enabling arbitrary text-driven attribute modifications. DreamMix introduces three key components: (i) an Attribute Decoupling Mechanism (ADM) that synthesizes diverse attribute-augmented image-text pairs to mitigate overfitting; (ii) a Textual Attribute Substitution (TAS) module that suppresses residual source attributes via orthogonal decomposition, and (iii) a Disentangled Inpainting Framework (DIF) that separates local generation from global harmonization. Extensive experiments across multiple inpainting backbones demonstrate that DreamMix achieves a superior balance between identity preservation and attribute editability across diverse applications, including object insertion, attribute editing, and small object inpainting.

title: RDD: Improving Structure from Motion with a Robust Feature Detector and Descriptor
abstract: Abstract Robust feature detection and description are core components of 3D vision pipelines, yet they remain challenging under large viewpoint, scale, and appearance changes. Recent methods have improved local feature learning, but many still rely on convolutional operators whose local receptive fields limit their ability to capture long-range geometric cues. We present Robust Deformable Detector (RDD), a robust keypoint detector and descriptor that uses deformable transformers to capture global context and geometric invariance. Deformable attention allows the descriptor branch to focus on a sparse set of informative locations, reducing the effective search space while preserving the ability to model long-range relationships. We also collect an Air-to-Ground dataset for training and evaluation, complementing the standard MegaDepth dataset. RDD outperforms state-of-the-art keypoint detection and description methods in sparse matching and also supports semi-dense matching. To support comprehensive evaluation, we introduce two challenging benchmarks: MegaDepth-View, which emphasizes large viewpoint and scale variations, and Air-to-Ground, which targets cross-altitude matching for 3D reconstruction. Project page: https://xtcpete.github.io/rdd/ .

title: HR-INR: Continuous Space-Time Video Super-Resolution via Event Camera
abstract: Abstract Continuous space-time video super-resolution (C-STVSR) aims to simultaneously enhance video resolution and frame rate at an arbitrary scale. Recently, implicit neural representation (INR) has been applied to video restoration, representing videos as implicit fields that can be decoded at an arbitrary scale. However, existing INR-based C-STVSR methods typically rely on only two frames as input, leading to insufficient inter-frame motion information. Consequently, they struggle to capture fast, complex motion and long-term dependencies (spanning more than three frames), hindering their performance in dynamic scenes. In this paper, we propose a novel C-STVSR framework, named HR-INR, which captures both h olistic dependencies and r egional motions based on INR. It is assisted by an event camera – a novel sensor renowned for its high temporal resolution and low latency. To fully utilize the rich temporal information from events, we design a feature extraction consisting of (1) a regional event feature extractor – taking events as inputs via the proposed event temporal pyramid representation to capture the regional nonlinear motion and (2) a holistic event-frame feature extractor for long-term dependence and continuity motion. We then propose a novel INR-based decoder with spatiotemporal embeddings to capture long-term dependencies with a larger temporal perception field. We validate the effectiveness and generalization of our method on four datasets (both simulated and real data), showing the superiority of our method. The project page is available at https://github.com/yunfanLu/HR-INR .

title: Privacy Leakage on DNNs: A Survey of Model Inversion Attacks and Defenses
abstract: Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) have revolutionized various domains with their exceptional performance across numerous applications. However, Model Inversion (MI) attacks, which disclose private information about the training dataset by abusing access to the trained models, have emerged as a formidable privacy threat. Given a trained network, these attacks enable adversaries to reconstruct high-fidelity data that closely aligns with the private training samples, posing significant privacy concerns. Despite the rapid advances in the field, we lack a comprehensive and systematic overview of existing MI attacks and defenses. To fill this gap, this paper thoroughly investigates this realm and presents a holistic survey. Firstly, our work briefly reviews early MI studies on traditional machine learning scenarios. We then elaborately analyze and compare numerous recent attacks and defenses on Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) across multiple modalities and learning tasks. By meticulously analyzing their distinctive features, we summarize and classify these methods into different categories and provide a novel taxonomy. Finally, this paper discusses promising research directions and presents potential solutions to open issues. To facilitate further study on MI attacks and defenses, we have implemented an open-source model inversion toolbox on GitHub .

title: Efficient Test-Time Prompt Tuning for Vision-Language Models
abstract: Vision-language models have showcased impressive zero-shot classification capabilities when equipped with suitable text prompts. Previous studies have shown the effectiveness of test-time prompt tuning; however, these methods often require per-image prompt adaptation during inference, which is computationally intensive and limits scalability and deployment. To address this issue, we introduce a novel framework: Self-supervised learning for efficient Test-time Prompt Tuning (Self-TPT). The key feature of Self-TPT is its shift to efficient predefined class adaptation through self-supervision, thereby avoiding the computation-heavy per-image adaptation at inference. Self-TPT starts by co-training the self-supervised and supervised tasks using source data, and then applies the self-supervision exclusively for new class understanding before making predictions. Specifically, we propose Contrastive Prompt Learning (CPT) as the core task for self-supervision. CPT is designed to minimize the intra-class distances while enhancing inter-class distinguishability via contrastive learning. Empirical evidence suggests that CPT can partially mimic supervised learning in terms of gradients, providing a plausible explanation for its effectiveness. Motivated by this finding, we introduce a gradient matching loss to explicitly enhance gradient similarity. We evaluated Self-TPT across three challenging zero-shot benchmarks. The results consistently show that Self-TPT not only significantly reduces inference costs but also achieves state-of-the-art performance, effectively balancing the efficiency-efficacy trade-off.

title: Ultra-High-Definition Image Restoration via Prior-driven Patch Bilateral Compensation
abstract: Advances in mobile imaging enable smartphones to capture 4K UHD images with rich detail, yet real-world degradations such as moiré patterns, rain streaks, and low-light noise make UHD restoration challenging. Existing methods are often computationally and memory intensive at UHD scale and underutilize degradation-specific cues and internal statistics under resource constraints, limiting faithful detail recovery and global structural consistency. We propose P rior-driven P atch-based Bi lateral C ompensation ( P2BiC ), a memory-efficient UHD restoration framework that processes UHD images as patches via an in-network feature-space cropping computation path while maintaining global coherence. Our key insight is that task-specific priors extracted from the observation can exhibit a higher structure-to-artifact ratio than the raw degraded input, whereas the degraded input still provides reliable global tone statistics even under color shifts, which is critical to suppress tone drift and boundary seams in patch-based UHD inference. Accordingly, we introduce prior-guided detail transfer to transfer structure-oriented cues from priors for detail reconstruction and style-aware tone adjustment to align tonal consistency across patches for coherent color. Extensive experiments show that P2BiC achieves strong quality on UHD image demoiréing, deraining, and low-light enhancement, with improved memory scalability.

title: CLIDD: Cross-Layer Independent Deformable Description for Efficient and Discriminative Local Feature Representation
abstract: Robust local feature representations are essential for spatial intelligence tasks such as robot navigation and augmented reality. Establishing reliable correspondences requires descriptors that provide both high discriminative power and computational efficiency. To address this, we introduce Cross-Layer Independent Deformable Description (CLIDD), a method that achieves superior discriminability by sampling directly from independent feature hierarchies. This approach utilizes learnable offsets to capture fine-grained structural details across scales, without ever constructing a unified dense feature map, eliminating the memory and computation overhead of building a full-scale representation for a sparse sampling process. The per-keypoint per-layer offsets further break interpolation-induced correlation, preserving descriptor discriminability even at high keypoint densities. To ensure real-time performance, we implement a hardware-aware kernel fusion strategy that maximizes inference throughput. Furthermore, we develop a scalable framework that integrates lightweight architectures with a training protocol leveraging both metric learning and knowledge distillation. This scheme generates a wide spectrum of model variants optimized for diverse deployment constraints. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that our approach achieves superior matching accuracy and exceptional computational efficiency simultaneously. Specifically, the ultra-compact variant matches the precision of SuperPoint while utilizing only 0.004M parameters, achieving a 99.7% reduction in model size. Furthermore, our high-performance configuration outperforms a broad range of current state-of-the-art methods, including high-capacity DINOv2-based frameworks, while exceeding 200 FPS on edge devices. These results demonstrate that CLIDD delivers high-precision local feature matching with minimal computational overhead, providing a robust and scalable solution for real-time spatial intelligence tasks.

title: MC-PanDA++: Simpler, Stronger, and More Robust Domain-Adaptive Panoptic Segmentation
abstract: Unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) reduces the annotation burden in panoptic segmentation by leveraging a cost-effectively labeled source domain (e.g., synthetic) and an unlabeled target domain to bridge the distribution gap. Existing panoptic UDA methods rely on teacher-student consistency learning built upon suboptimal per-pixel segmentation architectures. In contrast, state-of-the-art mask transformers are rarely adopted due to their pronounced vulnerability to confirmation bias in consistency learning, where erroneous teacher predictions are reinforced during training. Our earlier approach, MC-PanDA (Martinović et al., 2024), mitigates this issue through fine-grained confidence estimation, which suppresses gradients from unreliable masks while sampling informative yet reliable locations for loss computation. However, this method entails a complex multi-stage training and requires careful hyperparameter tuning. This work presents MC-PanDA ++ , which addresses these limitations by introducing: (i) self-supervised vision encoders that provide a stronger and more robust initialization, further reducing the reliance on human annotations, (ii) per-class, self-adapting mask-wide loss scaling that stabilizes training and enables the use of a single set of hyperparameters across domains, and (iii) a single-stage training pipeline that significantly decreases overall conceptual complexity. Together, these improvements result in a conceptually simpler, better-performing, and more robust method for domain-adaptive panoptics. We will release the source code and checkpoints.

title: Boundary-Aware Model with Deformable Feature Warping for Sparse-View Reconstruction
abstract: Recently, Large Reconstruction Models (LRMs) have shown impressive results. Existing feed-forward methods lift 2D to 3D via the extraction of global context information from input views. However, the issues in view feature extraction and geometric extraction in previous methods inevitably lead to low-quality surface reconstruction. Specifically, in view feature extraction, they do not leverage boundary and spatial information of shape within input views when modeling geometric relationships and neglect inconsistencies among view features. In geometric extraction, they are hampered by the inflexibility of geometric fittings that convert high-quality meshes from signed distance field (SDF). In this work, we propose B oundary- A ware L arge R econstruction M odel (BA-LRM) to tackle these issues for high-quality reconstruction. Our key contributions are three-fold: (1) Boundary-Aware Feature Extraction: We utilize a hierarchical segmentation model to extract boundary information from view images, enhanced with adapter modules to simultaneously capture spatial information, ensuring the extraction of boundary-aware and spatial-aware view features. (2) View Feature Deformation: We present an adaptive view feature deformation (AFD) to mitigate inconsistencies among view features. (3) Mesh Extraction and Geometric Constraints: To achieve better mesh quality, we employ a non-linear mesh extraction based on the Closest Point Transform. Additionally, SDF based on winding number is used for ground truth SDF extraction. It provides precise geometric constraints during training. Experimental results demonstrate that BA-LRM significantly outperforms existing sparse-view LRMs with the same volume of training data in terms of geometry quality and efficiency.

title: Blurring Modal Boundaries: A Unified Survey from Single- to Multi-modal Person Re-ldentification
abstract: Person re-identification (ReID) serves as a critical component in intelligent surveillance systems, aiming to match identities across disjoint camera networks. While traditional methods primarily rely on single-modal RGB imagery, they are often constrained by environmental challenges such as low illumination and occlusion. To overcome these limitations, the field is rapidly evolving toward cross-modal and multi-modal paradigms. This survey presents a comprehensive overview of this transition, systematically reviewing key cross-modal tasks including visible-infrared (VI-ReID), text-image (TI-ReID), sketch-based (Sketch-ReID), and the emerging Non-Line-of-Sight (NLOS) ReID, which extends perception beyond direct visibility. Furthermore, we examine tri-spectral and multi-modal fusion ReID, discussing how complementary information from diverse sensors enhances robustness. Beyond summarizing datasets, challenges, and methodologies, we propose a Transformer-based baseline framework for visible-infrared ReID, designed to effectively capture modality-invariant features. Finally, based on the current landscape, we outline several promising directions for future research.

title: Semantic Privacy Protection with Utility Preservation for 3D Point Clouds
abstract: Abstract Point cloud data face serious semantic privacy risks during acquisition, transmission, and cross-institutional sharing. Existing methods mostly rely on geometric perturbation or destructive encryption, which can reduce the recognizability of the original class but often impair downstream usability. This paper proposes a class-transfer-based semantic encryption framework for point clouds, aiming to conceal original class information while preserving task utility and supporting authorized recovery. Specifically, we construct a unified latent space with a shared-backbone Normalizing Flow, and combine LoRA and FiLM to achieve parameter-efficient class-conditional adaptation. We further introduce diffusion-guided flow alignment to regularize the latent distribution, construct an energy-based category transition graph, and obtain an optimal class-transfer table through global matching. Then, a latent-space Neural ODE continuously evolves source-class latents into target-class latents, which are decoded into target-class point clouds through the inverse flow. We adopt attacker-oriented metrics, including New-Class Recognition Rate (NCRR), Original-Class Leakage Rate (OCLR), and Original Label Recovery Rate (OLRR), to evaluate privacy and utility. Experiments on classification and segmentation benchmarks show that the proposed method achieves controllable semantic transformation, effectively reduces original-class semantic leakage, preserves downstream learnability in the protected domain, and supports reliable authorized reconstruction.

title: RS-vHeat+: An Efficient Remote Sensing Foundation Model Guided by Multi-Modal Fine-Grained Visual Semantics via Heat Conduction
abstract: Remote sensing foundation models (RSFMs) benefit greatly from large-scale pretraining, yet existing architectures still face two fundamental limitations: (1) the lack of computationally efficient and physically interpretable mechanisms for modeling global spatial interactions, and (2) a persistent semantic gap caused by weak fine-grained supervision during pretraining, which restricts their transferability to object-level downstream tasks. To address these, inspired by heat conduction, we model remote sensing image computation as a local heat diffusion process. We propose RS-vHeat+, an efficient multi-modal remote sensing foundation model (RSFM) for optical and SAR data, employing the heat conduction operator to propagate structural features while maintaining a global receptive field and reducing computational complexity to \(O(N^{1.5})\) . Furthermore, to narrow the semantic gap to downstream tasks, we introduce patch-level fine-grained semantic supervision during pretraining, which encourages the encoder to learn discriminative object-level cues. Pretrained on a 3.28-million multi-modal dataset, RS-vHeat+ demonstrates strong generalization across 12 benchmarks spanning object detection, semantic segmentation, change detection, classification, and SAR interpretation. Notably, compared with transformer-based RSFMs, RS-vHeat+ reduces memory usage by 84%, lowers FLOPs by 24%, and achieves 2.7 \(\times \) higher throughput, while demonstrating competitive performance against state-of-the-art methods on both coarse- and fine-grained tasks. Code is available at https://github.com/iecashhy/RS-vHeat .

title: Socialality Anchors: Towards Group-Bounded Trajectory Prediction
abstract: Trajectory prediction is a key component for understanding human behavior patterns in dynamic scenes. Researchers have devoted substantial efforts to modeling social interactions, especially group-wise interactions, since group membership often reflects shared intention, coordinated motion, and stable mutual adaptation, thus providing a persistent and semantically meaningful social prior for forecasting. However, existing group modeling methods may rely on a fixed threshold and infer groups mainly from agents’ relative positions within the observation window, overlooking the fact that grouping rules should be agent-specific, temporally coherent, and context-adaptive across diverse personalities, culturalities, and evolving interaction contexts. Inspired by human social perception that alternates between interpersonal distance in boundary-sensitive situations and relative speed consistency in dynamic interactions, we propose Socialality , a human-inspired trajectory prediction framework with interpretable socialality anchors and an extended grouping window for stable, context-aware grouping inference. Concretely, Socialality introduces a duo-scalar-controlled grouping kernel Socialality that jointly leverages historical observations and short-term future trajectory previews to learn agent-specific grouping rules, and employs a group-wise perception mechanism to model in-group and out-of-group interactions in an intuitive and explainable manner. Furthermore, we conduct extensive experiments on standard benchmarks to demonstrate the performance gains of Socialality , and provide qualitative analyses and statistical studies of anchor distributions to verify the interpretability and stability of the proposed socialality anchors. Code repo: https://github.com/LivepoolQ/Socialality

title: SLCA++: Unleash the Power of Sequential Fine-Tuning for Continual Learning with Pre-training
abstract: With the growing use of pre-trained models in modern vision systems, continual learning with pre-training (CLPT) has become a practically important paradigm for learning sequential downstream tasks while preserving and reusing pre-trained knowledge. While many recent CLPT methods rely on task-specific prompts or other auxiliary modules, we revisit a simpler and more fundamental baseline: sequential fine-tuning (Seq FT). We identify the key challenge for Seq FT in CLPT is progressive overfitting , where overly aggressive representation updates impair the transferability of pre-trained knowledge, while disjointly learned classifiers introduce additional bias across tasks. To address the challenge, we first present an optimization-oriented analysis based on Local Compatibility Property (LCP) for the learning of representation, which leads to Slow Learner for stabilizing representation updates over time. Specifically, Slow Learner improves optimization stability by controlling the learning rate of the representation layer, together with an additional symmetric cross-entropy objective to better balance gradient contributions from different training samples. We further show that Seq FT remains effective with substantially fewer updated parameters when backbone-native lightweight parameters are jointly optimized with pre-train-derived low-rank updates to attention and feed-forward weights. To resolve the remaining discrepancy between disjoint classifiers, a Classifier Alignment is introduced, which post-hoc calibrates the classifier using class-wise feature statistics. Extensive experiments across class-incremental and domain-incremental benchmarks, under both supervised and self-supervised pre-training, show that our method (SLCA++) consistently yields large gains over plain Seq FT baseline, while substantially narrowing the gap to joint training. These results suggest that carefully stabilized sequential fine-tuning can serve as a simple, strong, and informative baseline for continual learning with pre-training. Our code is available at: https://github.com/GengDavid/SLCA .

title: CorrCLIPv2: Harnessing Unlabeled Images for Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation
abstract: Open-vocabulary semantic segmentation aims to classify pixels without being restricted to a fixed set of categories. Although Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP) demonstrates remarkable potential for open-vocabulary recognition, its segmentation capability is impaired by unconstrained inter-class patch aggregation. To this end, this work proposes a unified training-free object-centric framework, named CorrCLIPv2, from three complementary aspects of patch correlation, feature representation, and output regularization. Specifically, for patch correlation, we leverage class-agnostic mask generators to explicitly disentangle inter-class interactions. Moreover, we utilize spatially-coherent features from self-supervised models to compute attention scores to mitigate mask inaccuracies. Regarding feature representation, we devise a refinement mechanism to simultaneously strengthen spatial details and semantic representation. Within the output space, we unify predictions via voting in each mask to enhance spatial consistency. To mitigate contextual bias and enhance prediction accuracy of objects, we further extend the framework by incorporating a cross-image object retrieval paradigm, which incurs minimal computational overhead. We build a memory bank of CorrCLIP-enhanced features from unlabeled images and implement a regime of multi-CLIP ensemble. By aggregating semantically consistent object features across diverse contexts retrieved from the memory bank, CorrCLIPv2 mitigates context-induced interference and obtains more robust predictions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach achieves the best or tied-best results among training-free methods on 10 standard benchmarks, surpassing some fully supervised methods on individual benchmarks. Remarkably, on the 22-dataset multi-domain MESS benchmark it further exhibits stronger cross-domain robustness than fully supervised open-vocabulary methods. Code is available at: https://github.com/zdk258/CorrCLIP .

title: Efficient Time-Fractional Diffusion Network for Under-Display ToF Imaging and Beyond
abstract: Under-display ToF imaging aims to both achieve precise depth sensing and maximize user experience by embedding a ToF camera beneath a screen panel. However, multiple complex degradations may occur during the imaging process, resulting in significant deterioration of depth quality. To alleviate this drawback, we introduce a hybrid framework, named Learnable Fractional Reaction–Diffusion Dynamics (LFRD \(^2\) ), which integrates the robust feature representation capabilities of neural networks with the interpretability of physical models. Specifically, we design a neural module implementing the time-fractional reaction–diffusion equation, which allows for iterative refinement to enhance depth quality, whose differential orders are generated dynamically. This module can correlate the current state of the predicted depth with any preceding states, keeping track of the long-term memory of the system itself. To further enhance computational efficiency and obtain a compact recursive realization of fractional dynamics, we extend the formulation with a Caputo–Fabrizio-based fractional derivative, whose exponentially decaying kernel enables a single-step recursive implementation while preserving long-memory characteristics. Moreover, we introduce an efficient continuous convolution approximation that combines repeated differentiation with learnable coefficient prediction, enabling a parametric representation of continuous kernel operators while maintaining computational efficiency. Extensive experiments on five benchmark datasets, including both synthetic and real UD-ToF data, classical ToF denoising, and depth super-resolution, illustrate the effectiveness of our framework. The code will be made available upon acceptance.

title: Benchmarking Large Language Models for Video Quality Assessment: Structured Perceptual Prompting and Refinement
abstract: Video Quality Assessment (VQA) is a pivotal yet challenging task in multimedia systems, owing to the complex interplay between perceptual and content-related factors. Despite the remarkable reasoning capabilities exhibited by Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) across diverse domains, their application to VQA remains largely underexplored. In this paper, we investigate the potential of MLLMs for VQA tasks and introduce a structured perceptual prompting and refinement pipeline that systematically evaluates video quality. Inspired by human perceptual processes, the proposed CoT framework adopts a hierarchical and sequential approach, which progressively addresses the video content analysis, perceptual quality, temporal distortion, and overall quality dimensions. Additionally, a refinement stage grounded in double-stimulus psychology is introduced to ensure a robust relative ranking, subsequently refining the quality predictions. We conduct a comprehensive study of nine prominent MLLMs (i.e., GPT-4o, GPT-5.1, Gemini-1.5-Pro, Gemini-3-Pro, Qwen2-VL, Qwen3-VL-Plus, Claude-Sonnet-4.5, Grok 4, and LLaVA-video) on three benchmark VQA datasets using both standard and CoT prompting strategies. Experimental results reveal that, under standard prompting, only GPT-4o, GPT-5.1, and Qwen3-VL-Plus achieve reasonable performance compared to existing state-of-the-art (SOTA) unsupervised VQA methods. Notably, the proposed CoT framework effectively enhances the performance of all evaluated MLLMs, where GPT-5.1 outperforms the existing SOTA (SRCC: 0.781 vs. 0.760, PLCC: 0.792 vs. 0.761).

title: GoClick: Lightweight Element Grounding Model for Autonomous GUI Interaction
abstract: Graphical User Interface (GUI) element grounding−precisely locating elements on screenshots based on natural language instructions−is fundamental for agents interacting with GUIs. Deploying this capability directly on resource-constrained devices like mobile phones is increasingly critical for GUI agents requiring low latency. However, this goal faces a significant challenge, as current visual grounding methods typically employ large vision-language model (VLM) ( \(\ge 2.5\) B parameters), making them impractical for on-device execution due to memory and computational constraints. To address this, this paper introduces GoClick , a lightweight GUI element grounding VLM with only 230 M parameters that achieves excellent visual grounding accuracy, even on par with significantly larger models. Simply downsizing existing decoder-only VLMs is a straightforward way to design a lightweight model, but our experiments reveal that this approach yields suboptimal results. Instead, we select an encoder-decoder architecture, which outperforms decoder-only alternatives at small parameter scales for GUI grounding tasks. Additionally, the limited capacity of small VLMs encourages us to develop a Progressive Data Refinement pipeline that utilizes task type filtering and data ratio adjustment to extract a high-quality 3.8M-sample core set from a 10.8M raw dataset. Training GoClick using this core set brings notable grounding accuracy gains. Our experiments show that GoClick excels on multiple GUI element grounding benchmarks while maintaining a small size and high inference speed. GoClick also enhances GUI agent performance when integrated into a device-cloud collaboration framework, where GoClick helps cloud-based task planners perform precise element localization and achieve higher success rates. We hope our method serves as a meaningful exploration within the GUI agent community.

title: LLM-Powered Query Expansion for Enhancing Boundary Prediction in Language-Driven Action Localization
abstract: Language-driven action localization in videos requires not only semantic alignment between language query and video segment, but also prediction of action boundaries. However, the language query primarily describes the main content of an action and usually lacks specific details of action start and end boundaries, which increases the subjectivity of manual boundary annotation and leads to boundary uncertainty in training data. In this paper, on one hand, we propose to expand the original query by generating textual descriptions of the action start and end boundaries through LLMs, which can provide more detailed boundary cues for localization and thus reduce the impact of boundary uncertainty. On the other hand, to enhance the tolerance to boundary uncertainty during training, we propose to model probability scores of action boundaries by calculating the semantic similarities between frames and the expanded query as well as the temporal distances between frames and the annotated boundary frames. They can provide more consistent boundary supervision, thus improving the stability of training. Our method is model-agnostic and can be seamlessly and easily integrated into any existing models of language-driven action localization in an off-the-shelf manner. Experimental results on several datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our method.

title: Event-Guided Decomposition from a Long-Exposure Nighttime Snapshot into Video Sequence
abstract: Nighttime videography struggles with a dilemma between severe motion blur and low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). To bypass this challenge, we propose an event-guided blur decomposition network (EBDNet) built on RGB-event hybrid photography, which captures long-exposure RGB images with decent SNR alongside an event stream reflecting fast dynamics, and aggregates them to reconstruct sharp motion sequences computationally. The EBDNet incorporates an implicit temporal representation to recursively model frame evolution and progressively reconstruct the latent video sequence. For effective model training, we design a two-stage optimization strategy, where the first stage establishes a reconstruction foundation using paired data, and the second stage further enhances generalization to scenarios without ground-truth supervision through additional consistency constraints. By leveraging the complementary data from the two sensors and applying a sophisticated fusion technique, EBDNet resolves ambiguities in motion direction and allows precise decomposition of complex motion blur. Comprehensive experiments conducted in both synthetic and real-world low-light scenarios demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms existing techniques. This proposed approach provides a robust solution for high-quality video recording in dark environments and holds significant potential for nighttime surveillance and navigation.

title: Test-Time Computing for Referring Multimodal Large Language Models
abstract: We propose ControlMLLM++ , a novel test-time adaptation framework that injects learnable visual prompts into frozen multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to enable fine-grained region-based visual reasoning without any model retraining or fine-tuning. Leveraging the insight that cross-modal attention maps intrinsically encode semantic correspondences between textual tokens and visual regions, ControlMLLM++ optimizes a latent visual token modifier during inference via a task-specific energy function to steer model attention towards user-specified areas. To enhance optimization stability and mitigate language prompt biases, ControlMLLM++ incorporates an improved optimization strategy (Optim++) and a prompt debiasing mechanism (PromptDebias). Supporting diverse visual prompt types including bounding boxes, masks, scribbles, and points, our method demonstrates strong out-of-domain generalization and interpretability. The code is available at https://github.com/mrwu-mac/ControlMLLM .

title: Multi-View Optimal Transport for Multi-View Crowd Localization and Tracking
abstract: Multi-view crowd localization and tracking aim to predict the ground-plane positions of all individuals in the scene and estimate their trajectories over time. Existing multi-view localization methods typically rely on Gaussian-smoothed density map supervision, whose inherent ambiguity in crowded regions may blur local peaks and degrade localization accuracy. In this work, we introduce a multi-view optimal transport framework that directly supervises point-level predictions on the ground plane, thereby avoiding the limitations of density map regression. Specifically, we propose a Mahalanobis distance-based multi-view optimal transport loss (M-MVOT), whose transport cost incorporates view ray direction and object-to-camera distance within a Mahalanobis formulation, with the direction guiding the ellipse orientation and the distance modulating the cost magnitude. For multi-view tracking, we first extend the proposed localization framework in a tracking-by-detection manner (MVOT-TBD). To further improve performance, we introduce a tracking-specific optimal transport loss (MVOT-Track) that explicitly supervises inter-frame association. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed optimal transport-based framework consistently outperforms density map-based localization and tracking on multiple multi-view crowd datasets.

title: Learning Complex Scene Segmentation from Noisy Label
abstract: The development of deep learning techniques and the increasing scale of training set have led to breakthroughs in image segmentation. However, in complex segmentation scenarios, such as those involving camouflaged, densely structured, or pathological objects, the severe lack of annotations presents a significant obstacle to further progress. Although weakly supervised methods offer higher annotation efficiency, the inherent noise in weak annotations poses significant challenges to model optimization within such complex scenarios, resulting in suboptimal performance. Inspired by the information richness provided by different types of weak annotations, we explore the potential of incorporating boxes into the training process. Treating box annotations as prompts, we introduce a Weakly Semi-Supervised Object Segmentation (WSSOS) training paradigm, which aims to achieve low-cost, high-precision object segmentation with only a minimal number of pixel-level annotations. Nevertheless, we identify two key challenges in WSSOS: selecting the most valuable samples for annotation using only box annotations, and improving learning performance on noisy pseudo-labels. To address these challenges, we propose two corresponding solutions: a sample selection method based on Maximum Spatial Distance (MSD), and a noise correction loss \(\mathcal {L}_{NC}\) . Specifically, the MSD algorithm assesses sample significance by quantifying the distinctions between foreground and background regions, while employing spatial distance metrics for sample selection, thereby guaranteeing both the diversity and representativeness of the constructed coreset. \(\mathcal {L}_{NC}\) helps the model learn the correct pixels during the early learning stage, and corrects gradient errors induced by noisy pixels during the memory stage, ultimately enabling accurate object segmentation from noisy labels. We validate the effectiveness of the proposed method on three challenging tasks, and demonstrate that, when only 20% of fully labeled data is available, our method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches. Our code is available at https://github.com/zhangjinCV/NoisyWSSOS .

title: LexSign: Learning Sign Language from Lexical Descriptions
abstract: Understanding fine-grained human actions is crucial for bridging visual perception and linguistic reasoning, especially in sign languages, where meaning is encoded through structured visual-spatial subunits. However, existing sign language understanding (SLU) methods rely on coarse-grained gloss annotations or costly expert-designed symbolic systems, limiting fine-grained modeling and generalization. In this work, we investigate lexical descriptions as an intermediate linguistic representation for SLU. Specifically, we first construct LexSign, a large-scale dataset of approximately 4,000 glosses comprising both manually curated and automatically generated lexical descriptions of signs. We further design LexSign-Bench, a benchmark covering 600 glosses to evaluate the SLU capabilities of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) at both gloss and subunit levels. To exploit the hierarchical structure of lexical descriptions, we propose a Hierarchical Action-Language Interaction (HALI) framework with multi-granularity contrastive alignment and cross-level consistency constraints. Extensive evaluations reveal a substantial gap between MLLMs and humans, regardless of sign language experience. Furthermore, experiments on public and newly constructed datasets demonstrate that HALI learns more discriminative and generalizable representations across multiple SLU tasks, including zero-shot sign language recognition, isolated sign language recognition, and sign language spotting. These results highlight the critical role of linguistically grounded knowledge in advancing scalable and fine-grained SLU.

title: PASG-RoboKeyBench: A Closed-Loop Automated Framework and Benchmark for Operation Primitive Extraction and Semantic Anchoring in Robotic Manipulation
abstract: Developing generalizable robotic manipulation for open-world tasks requires precise understanding of operation primitives–key points and axes–that bridge high-level task semantics and low-level interaction poses. Despite advances in multimodal large language models (MLLMs), current approaches face intertwined challenges: (1) Scalability limitations due to dependency on manual annotation for primitive-semantic grounding, and (2) Evaluation gaps from the absence of dedicated benchmarks assessing fine-grained intra-object spatial reasoning. To overcome these, we propose Primitive-Aware Semantic Grounding (PASG), an automated closed-loop framework that establishes hierarchical geometric-to-functional semantics for robotic primitives. PASG synergizes geometry-aware primitive extraction with MLLM-based dynamic semantic anchoring, implementing self-corrective loops to continuously refine primitive-semantic alignment without human intervention. Complementing this, we introduce RoboKeyBench, the first benchmark designed for holistic evaluation of MLLMs’ operation primitive comprehension. It features 14,958 visual question answering samples organized hierarchically (geometry \(\rightarrow \) function \(\rightarrow \) manipulation) across 5731 objects. Rigorous evaluation of state-of-the-art MLLMs reveals significant performance disparities, empirically pinpointing critical capability boundaries in geometric abstraction and functional grounding. Our contributions deliver: (i) A manual-annotation-free framework (PASG) for closed-loop automated semantic anchoring; (ii) A hierarchical foundational-capability benchmark (RoboKeyBench) for operation primitive evaluation; and (iii) Actionable insights for refining both MLLMs and manipulation architectures.

title: Zero-Shot Domain Generalization via Domain Prompt Learning
abstract: Domain generalization (DG) aims to improve the generalization of the model to any unseen domains. Targeting this goal, existing DG methods mainly focus on learning domain-invariant features or prompts from the given source domains. However, these methods rely on source-domain data, and collecting and annotating large-scale single- or multi-source datasets is often infeasible, limiting the practical applicability of DG. To tackle this challenge, we propose Domain Prompt Learning (DoP), a method built on a large vision-language model (e.g., CLIP) for zero-shot domain generalization, which recognizes unseen classes in unseen target domains without access to source-domain data. DoP essentially learns the target domain knowledge via prompt both in text and visual modalities to overcome the domain shift in text-visual modalities under the test-time adaptation formulation. Specifically, DoP first takes text domain learning (TDL) to simulate various distribution shifts by learning diverse style tokens implicitly in the text space with inter-style diversity loss and intra-style consistency loss. Subsequently, DoP employs visual domain learning (VDL) to further refine the target-domain-relevant style token generated by TDL by making use of the test visual data with self-supervised learning. Extensive experiments on popular DG benchmark datasets (e.g., PACS, VLCS, OfficeHome, and DomainNet) and ImageNet show that our DoP consistently outperforms the state-of-the-art DG approaches. Codes are available at: https://github.com/shiming-chen/DoP .

title: Cross3DReg: A Real-world Cross-source Point Cloud Registration Benchmark
abstract: Point cloud registration aligns point clouds acquired from different viewpoints or sensing devices. Cross-source point cloud registration specifically aims to align point clouds captured by heterogeneous LiDAR sensors with substantially divergent sampling patterns and densities. Compared to the same-source point cloud registration, cross-source registration faces two core challenges: the lack of publicly available real-world datasets for training the deep registration models and the inherent difference in point clouds captured by multiple sensors. The diverse patterns induced by sensors pose great challenges in robust and accurate point cloud feature extraction and matching, which negatively influence the registration accuracy. To address these challenges, we introduce Cross3DReg, a large-scale real-world outdoor benchmark collected using two heterogeneous LiDAR sensors: a rotating mechanical LiDAR and a hybrid semi-solid-state LiDAR. Moreover, an overlap-based cross-source registration framework is designed to utilize unaligned images to predict the overlapping region between the source and target. By filtering out redundant points in non-overlapping regions, the framework effectively reduces interference from noise and irrelevant points. Then, a visual-geometric attention guided matching module is proposed to enhance the consistency of cross-source point cloud features by fusing image and geometric information to establish reliable correspondences and ultimately achieve accurate and robust registration. Extensive experiments show that our method achieves state-of-the-art registration performance. Our framework reduces the relative rotational error and relative translational error to \(6.68^\circ \) and 1.01 m, respectively, and increases the registration recall to \(86.2\%\) , demonstrating its effectiveness in achieving cross-source point cloud registration.

title: BCP3D: Robust 3D Object Tracking Using Brain-Inspired Complementary-Pathway for Challenging Scenarios
abstract: Robust 3D object tracking using traditional cameras remains a significant challenge in scenarios involving rapid motion, poor illumination, cluttered backgrounds, and textureless objects, especially on embedded platforms that demand real-time performance under constrained compute. To address these limitations, we report on BCP3D, a complementary-pathway framework for 3D object tracking, leveraging the Tianmouc vision sensor. Tianmouc integrates two brain-inspired complementary pathways: a cognition-oriented pathway (COP) for precise color intensity sensing and an action-oriented pathway (AOP) for high-frame-rate spatiotemporal edge detection. We further propose a dual-pathway algorithm featuring cross-pathway integration, recurrent feedback loops, and multi-stage transfer to exploit complementary-pathway cues from Tianmouc efficiently. BCP3D leverages object probability maps from COP to extract the object’s contour while suppressing background textures in AOP’s edges, enabling robust contour-based pose optimization. An inter-pathway aligner allows pixel-level dual-pathway fusion and subsequent pose updates at AOP data frequency, yielding substantially finer temporal granularity of tracking. Additionally, an adaptive predictor dynamically modulates reliance on COP and the aligner, bypassing them in favor of AOP based on background complexity to optimize computational efficiency. To facilitate rigorous evaluation, we develop a robust ground truth annotation method and construct a comprehensive dataset encompassing extreme conditions, addressing the scarcity of dynamic textureless objects with motion blur in existing real-world datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that BCP3D achieves an average runtime of 2.08 ms on a laptop CPU with 94.7% tracking accuracy, outperforming state-of-the-art methods by over 35% tracking accuracy. These findings underscore the potential of brain-inspired sensing for efficient and robust 3D object tracking in challenging scenarios.

title: Synergizing Disentangled Representation and Split Federated Learning to Break Centralized Bottlenecks in Gaze Estimation
abstract: Mainstream appearance-based gaze estimation methods trained on centralized data are struggling in two urgent aspects. First, most gaze estimation methods require entire eye images or even full faces for model training, which raises serious concerns about the leakage of sensitive personal data. Second, simultaneously achieving generalization to unseen gaze data and personalization for individual subjects remains inherently conflicting to reconcile within a single centralized model. To break these bottlenecks, we propose SplitFedGaze, a distributed gaze estimation framework that synergizes the power of representation disentanglement and split federated learning. Instead of training a global model on centralized data, SplitFedGaze adopts a data-distributed, model-split optimization paradigm. Specifically, gaze-irrelevant components, which primarily involve personal privacy, are removed from the raw gaze data by a carefully designed disentangled information bottleneck module and are retained only on local clients. The desensitized representations, termed “gaze maps’’, encapsulate disentangled gaze-relevant information and are transmitted from local clients to a global server for gaze knowledge aggregation. To resolve the trade-off between generalization and personalization, the server-side gaze knowledge aggregator leverages gaze maps from all clients to enhance the global model’s generalizability. Furthermore, each local client is equipped with an exclusive personalized calibration module to mitigate performance degradation caused by physiological differences across subjects. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SplitFedGaze gains three remarkable advantages: (1) It achieves higher estimation accuracy than centralized and federated gaze estimation methods across various training settings. (2) It effectively mitigates the risk of gaze data leakage from reconstruction attacks. (3) It inherently supports personalized applications, overcoming inter-subject variability. Complementary experiments quantify deployment cost, privacy-utility trade-offs, few-shot adaptation, cross-dataset generalization, and update-level privacy mechanisms via differential privacy (DP) and secure aggregation.

title: Eyegent: Visual Attention Orchestration on Concepts
abstract: Abstract Where a human looks is not random, nor is it merely a reflex to visual salience. It is a decision shaped by goals, constrained by language, and driven by the need to resolve uncertainty. We propose Eyegent , an active vision agent built on this premise: that visual search is best understood as sequential Bayesian inference over semantically grounded hypotheses, with fixations serving as epistemic actions. Given an image and a natural-language query, Eyegent constructs a discrete hypothesis space of candidate segmentation masks, maintains an explicit posterior belief distribution, and selects each fixation to maximise expected information gain—updating beliefs via vision–language model verification and terminating when uncertainty falls below a principled risk threshold. We formalise this process as Bayesian Active Semantic Grounding (BASG), a computational-level account that provides formal guarantees on belief concentration, entropy reduction, and bounded decision risk. The framework is neurobiologically grounded in the large-scale network organisation of the human brain, with the Salience Network identified as the dynamic orchestrator of semantic, inferential, and oculomotor processes. Critically, Eyegent requires no gaze supervision and no task-specific training: it is zero-shot, modular, and built entirely from off-the-shelf components. Evaluated on RefCOCO-Gaze and AiR-D, two benchmarks coupling language-driven visual tasks with human eye-tracking ground truth, Eyegent achieves competitive or state-of-the-art performance among zero-shot methods across semantic, spatial, and structural scanpath metrics, and approaches supervised baselines on several dimensions. The result is a system that does not merely predict where humans look, but generates scanpaths for the same reason humans generate them: to find out.

title: $${\text {VLScene}}^{++}$$: Enhancing 3D Semantic Scene Completion via VLM Discrepancy-Aware Semantic Distillation and Sparse–Dense Hybrid Awareness
abstract: Camera-based 3D semantic scene completion (SSC) aims to infer dense geometric and semantic representations from limited visual observations, which remains challenging due to occlusions and perspective ambiguities. Although recent vision-language models (VLMs) provide rich high-level semantic knowledge, integrating such information into 3D SSC is non-trivial. A key challenge lies in the inaccurate fusion between dense, image-centric VLM semantics and sparse–dense voxel representations constrained by 3D geometry, often leading to semantic misalignment in weakly observed regions. To address this challenge, we propose \({\text {VLScene}}^{++}\) , a unified framework that enables geometry-consistent integration of VLM-derived semantic knowledge for 3D semantic scene completion. \({\text {VLScene}}^{++}\) introduces VLM Discrepancy-Aware Semantic Distillation to enhance image features with high-level semantic cues, improving spatial context reasoning while preserving geometry-related semantic structures during semantic feature learning. To further bridge the gap between sparse geometry and dense semantics, we design a Sparse–Dense Hybrid Awareness module with a dual-stream architecture. The Geometric-Semantic Sparse Awareness stream propagates reliable structural information in sparse 3D space, while the Dense Separable Context Refinement stream efficiently captures global semantic context. A Sparse-Guided Gated Fusion mechanism dynamically integrates these complementary representations. Extensive experiments on SemanticKITTI, SSCBench-KITTI-360, and nuScenes-Occupancy demonstrate that \({\text {VLScene}}^{++}\) achieves competitive performance against state-of-the-art methods in both geometric completion and semantic prediction.

title: TokLIP: Marry Visual Tokens to CLIP for Multimodal Comprehension and Generation
abstract: Abstract Pioneering token-based works such as Chameleon and Emu3 have established a foundation for multimodal unification but face challenges of high training computational overhead and limited comprehension performance due to a lack of high-level semantics. In this paper, we introduce TokLIP, a visual tokenizer that enhances comprehension by semanticizing vector-quantized (VQ) tokens and incorporating CLIP-level semantics while enabling end-to-end multimodal autoregressive training with standard VQ tokens. TokLIP integrates a low-level discrete VQ tokenizer with a ViT-based token encoder to capture high-level continuous semantics. Unlike previous approaches (e.g., VILA-U) that discretize high-level features, TokLIP disentangles training objectives for comprehension and generation, allowing the direct application of advanced VQ tokenizers without the need for tailored quantization operations. Our empirical results demonstrate that TokLIP achieves exceptional data efficiency, empowering visual tokens with high-level semantic understanding while enhancing low-level generative capacity, making it well-suited for autoregressive Transformers in both open-world comprehension and generation tasks. The code and models are available at https://github.com/TencentARC/TokLIP .

title: Inst-Inpaint: Instructing to Remove Objects with Diffusion Models
abstract: Abstract Image inpainting task refers to erasing unwanted pixels from images and filling them in a semantically consistent and realistic way. Traditionally, the pixels that are wished to be erased are defined with binary masks. From the application point of view, a user needs to generate the masks for the objects they would like to remove which can be time-consuming and prone to errors. In this work, we are interested in an image inpainting algorithm that estimates which object to be removed based on natural language input and removes it, simultaneously. For this purpose, first, we construct a dataset named GQA-Inpaint for this task. Second, we present an inpainting framework, Inst-Inpaint , that can remove objects from images based on the instructions given as text prompts. We set various GAN and diffusion-based baselines and run experiments on synthetic and real-world image datasets. We compare methods with different evaluation metrics that measure the quality and accuracy of the models and show significant quantitative and qualitative improvements. Please refer to the web page of the project for the released code and dataset: http://instinpaint.abyildirim.com/

title: SuperSVG++: Semantic-Driven Layer-Wise Scalable Vector Graphics Synthesis with Semantic Layer Decomposition
abstract: Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) is a widely used format due to its excellent scalability and editability. However, existing image vectorization methods either suffer from poor reconstruction quality for complex images or require excessive computation time, limiting their practical application. To address these challenges, we propose SuperSVG++, a semantic-driven, layer-wise vectorization model that converts raster images into SVG with high accuracy and efficiency. Firstly, SuperSVG++ proposes a semantic-aware hierarchical vectorization framework, which extracts and reorders semantic layers in a depth-aware manner, ensuring structured and semantic-aware vectorization. Furthermore, we propose a soft-hard boundary constraint in the semantic-aware coarse structure vectorization stage, which improves both the compactness and accuracy of vector paths. To refine details, we propose a difference-conditioned refinement model, which adaptively predicts refining paths based on a difference map computed between the rendered and target image. Additionally, we propose a layer-wise refinement strategy, utilizing a distance-aware priority queue to dynamically decompose and refine semantic regions in a coarse-to-fine and layer-wise manner. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SuperSVG++ outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both reconstruction accuracy and semantic consistency, achieving superior layer-wise vectorization performance.

title: Manhattan Gaussian Splatting SLAM
abstract: Recent neural and Gaussian-based SLAM systems have achieved impressive visual fidelity, yet reliable localization and mapping remain difficult in indoor environments with weak textures and repetitive geometric patterns. To solve the problem, we propose MGS-SLAM, a Manhattan-aware Gaussian Splatting SLAM framework that explicitly integrates structural priors into tracking, global pose graph optimization, and map refinement modules. First, we perform confidence-aware Manhattan rotation inference on SO (3) by propagating geometrically consistent surface normals from pivot keyframes and estimating dominant directions via von Mises–Fisher modeling. These estimates are fused with visual tracking through confidence-weighted rotation interpolation to ensure robustness under directional dominance. To curb drift over long trajectories, we further introduce a dual-manifold pose optimization module on \(SO(3)\times SO(3)\) , where Manhattan-aligned and world rotations are refined jointly under geometry-induced connectivity and anisotropic information weighting. Finally, Manhattan priors guide Gaussian densification and pruning, yielding structurally consistent maps. The scope of this work is static indoor RGB-D sequences. Experiments on Replica, TUM RGB-D and MP3D show that MGS-SLAM delivers robust localization and high-quality reconstruction in weakly textured and repetitive rooms, and that it compares favourably with recent neural and Gaussian-based SLAM systems while keeping a computational cost close to that of other differentiable-rendering pipelines.

title: Reconstruction and Restoration of 4D Light Fields via Super-resolved Inverse Image-Based Rendering
abstract: Light fields provide a powerful scene representation for photorealistic rendering effects such as digital refocusing, shallow depth-of-field, and novel view synthesis. However, acquiring high-density light fields remains impractical due to specialized hardware requirements and the inherent trade-off between spatial and angular resolution. To extend the benefits of light field representations to standard imaging setups, even under low-resolution sensing conditions, we propose Super-resolved Inverse Image-Based Rendering (SiIBR), a framework for reconstructing high-resolution 4D light fields from a single low-resolution RGB image. SiIBR formulates light field reconstruction as an inverse problem of image-based rendering and solves it by implementing the forward rendering process as a neural renderer. Within this inverse formulation, we incorporate a super-resolution mechanism at the level of Epipolar Plane Images (EPIs). As EPIs jointly encode spatial and angular dimensions, performing super-resolution in this domain enables the model to simultaneously enhance spatial resolution and enforce multi-view coherence, resulting in more accurate sub-pixel light flow estimation. Unlike conventional cascaded pipelines that first apply image super-resolution and then perform reconstruction, SiIBR directly infers dense light rays in 4D space. This ray-centric formulation yields a richer scene representation and inherently produces physically plausible anti-aliasing without explicit post-processing. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SiIBR consistently outperforms state-of-the-art novel view synthesis and light field reconstruction methods across multiple benchmarks. Notably, although trained exclusively on synthetic data, our approach generalizes well to diverse real-world datasets.

title: Event-Based Facial Expression Recognition via Knowledge-Enhanced Hypergraph Computation
abstract: Event cameras are bio-inspired vision sensors with high temporal resolution and high dynamic range. Recent years have witnessed great advancement in event cameras, and event-based facial expression recognition (FER) methods have demonstrated robustness to complex lighting conditions and gained wide attention. However, existing event-based FER methods are restricted to the naive usage of extracted global features for expression recognition and lack of analysis of detailed facial actions, resulting in insufficient recognition accuracy. To address this challenge, in this paper, we propose an event-based FER method based on knowledge-enhanced hypergraph computation. Our proposed method takes both events and frames as inputs to predict facial expressions. A high-dimensional feature interaction and extraction module is proposed to enhance multi-modal feature extraction by interacting in the high-dimensional nonlinear space. Subsequently, we propose a knowledge hypergraph-enhanced classification module, which models the spatial AUs-expression connections and the temporal correlations of AUs based on spatiotemporal hypergraphs, and uses the proposed weighted hypergraph convolution to achieve knowledge-based feature aggregation and scattering. By incorporating the knowledge into the features, more accurate FER can be effectively achieved. To prove the validity of our method, we conducted experiments on three large-scale datasets. The experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method achieves higher performance than existing methods. The ablation experiments further prove the effectiveness of each proposed module.

title: Reconstructing 4D Spatial Intelligence: A Survey
abstract: Reconstructing 4D spatial intelligence from visual observations has long been a central yet challenging task in computer vision, with broad real-world applications. These range from entertainment domains like movies, where the focus is often on reconstructing fundamental visual elements, to embodied AI, which emphasizes interaction modeling and physical realism. Fueled by rapid advances in 3D representations and deep learning architectures, the field has evolved quickly, outpacing the scope of previous surveys. Additionally, existing surveys rarely offer a comprehensive analysis of the hierarchical structure of 4D scene reconstruction. To address this gap, we present a new perspective that organizes existing methods into five progressive levels of 4D spatial intelligence: (1) Level 1—reconstruction of low-level 3D cues (e.g., depth, pose, and point maps); (2) Level 2—reconstruction of 3D scene components (e.g., objects, humans, structures); (3) Level 3—reconstruction of 4D dynamic scenes; (4) Level 4—modeling of interactions among scene components; and (5) Level 5 – physically grounded 4D reconstruction. We conclude the survey by discussing the key challenges at each level and highlighting promising directions for advancing toward even richer levels of 4D spatial intelligence. To track ongoing developments, we maintain an up-to-date project page: https://github.com/yukangcao/Awesome-4D-Spatial-Intelligence .

title: Performance Evaluation of Embedded AI Inference on Zynq Ultrascale+ and Versal SoCs for Onboard Space Applications
abstract: This work evaluates the performance of two Xilinx System-on-Chip (SoC) platforms, Zynq Ultrascale+ ( ZUS+ ) and Versal , for Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based onboard processing in space applications. The benchmarks focus on three distinct use cases: (1) ship detection on Earth observation data using a convolutional neural network model, (2) hazard detection and avoidance for asteroid landing missions with AI-based boulder segmentation, and (3) fault detection, isolation, and recovery through time-series analysis of inertial measurement unit (IMU) data. The Xilinx Vitis AI workflow is used to compile the models. Peta Linux is used on the Application Processing Unit (APU) of both SoCs, with OpenCV ( Python ) used for image pre-processing and Vitis AI Run Time ( VART ) libraries ( Python ) used to run the models and obtain the inferences. The study investigates processing speed, power efficiency, and thermal throttling (through cold starts) behavior under different conditions, as input data size and batch sizes. Results show that, despite being an older chip, ZUS+ excels in small-input scenarios with up to 80% faster processing and 66% lower energy per data processed than Versal . However, the latter outperforms the former for any larger inputs, with up to 358% faster processing and 66% lower energy per data processed with batch parallelization—without it, ZUS+ is still competitive. Across all scenarios, cold starts have a negligible performance impact (−0.02% for ZUS+ and −0.44% for Versal ). These findings provide key insights for selecting efficient SoCs for AI-driven autonomous operations in spacecraft, such as Earth observation, planetary landing, and fault detection.

title: EdgePoint2: Compact Descriptors for Superior Efficiency and Accuracy
abstract: The field of keypoint extraction, which is essential for vision applications like Structure from Motion (SfM) and Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM), has evolved from relying on handcrafted methods to leveraging deep learning techniques. While deep learning approaches have significantly improved performance, they often incur substantial computational costs, limiting their deployment in real-time edge applications. Efforts to create lightweight neural networks have seen some success, yet they often result in a trade-off between efficiency and accuracy. Additionally, the high-dimensional descriptors generated by these networks pose challenges for distributed applications requiring efficient communication and coordination, highlighting the need for compact yet competitively accurate descriptors. In this paper, we present EdgePoint2, a series of lightweight keypoint detection and description neural networks specifically tailored for edge computing applications on embedded systems. The network architecture is optimized for efficiency without sacrificing accuracy. To train compact descriptors, we introduce a combination of Orthogonal Procrustes loss and similarity loss, which can serve as a general approach for hypersphere embedding distillation tasks. Additionally, we offer 14 sub-models to satisfy diverse application requirements. Our experiments demonstrate that EdgePoint2 consistently achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) accuracy and efficiency across various challenging scenarios while employing lower-dimensional descriptors (32/48/64). Beyond its accuracy, EdgePoint2 offers significant advantages in flexibility, robustness, and versatility.
